maximum_subarray.brute:
best = nums[0]
for each start index:
    total = 0
    for each end index from start to n - 1:
        total = total + nums[end]
        if total > best: best = total
return best

jump_game_ii.brute:
jumps_to = array of n values -1, jumps_to[0] = 0
queue = [0]   (BFS, one level per jump)
while the queue is not empty:
    i = pop from the front of the queue
    if i == n - 1: return jumps_to[i]
    furthest = min(n - 1, i + nums[i])
    for each j from i + 1 to furthest:
        if jumps_to[j] == -1:
            jumps_to[j] = jumps_to[i] + 1
            append j to the queue
return jumps_to[n - 1]
jump_game_ii.optimal:
jumps = 0, current_end = 0, farthest = 0
for each index i from 0 to n - 2:
    if i + nums[i] > farthest: farthest = i + nums[i]
    if i == current_end:   (stepping off the current window: one more jump)
        jumps = jumps + 1
        current_end = farthest
return jumps

gas_station.brute:
for each start station:
    tank = 0, completed = true
    for each of the n steps around the circle:
        i = (start + step) mod n
        tank = tank + gas[i] - cost[i]
        if tank < 0: completed = false, break
    if completed: return start
return -1
gas_station.optimal:
total = 0, tank = 0, start = 0
for each station i:
    diff = gas[i] - cost[i]
    total = total + diff
    tank = tank + diff
    if tank < 0:   (no station from start to i can work: skip past i)
        start = i + 1, tank = 0
if total < 0: return -1
return start

number_of_1_bits.brute:
count = 0
for each bit position i from 0 to 31:
    bit = (n shifted right by i) AND 1
    if bit == 1: count = count + 1
return count
number_of_1_bits.optimal:
count = 0
while n != 0:
    n = n AND (n - 1)   (clears the lowest set bit)
    count = count + 1
return count

counting_bits.brute:
result = empty list
for each num from 0 to n:
    count = 0
    for each bit position b from 0 to 31:
        if bit b of num is set: count = count + 1
    append count to result
return result
counting_bits.optimal:
bits = n + 1 zeros
for each i from 1 to n:
    half = i shifted right by 1
    bits[i] = bits[half] + (lowest bit of i)   (drop one bit, reuse the smaller answer)
return bits

reverse_bits.brute:
bits = n written as a 32-character binary string
reversed_bits = bits read right to left
return reversed_bits parsed as a base-2 integer
reverse_bits.optimal:
result = 0
repeat 32 times:
    lowest = n AND 1
    result = (result shifted left by 1) OR lowest   (push the input's lowest bit onto the output)
    n = n shifted right by 1
return result

single_number.optimal:
result = 0
for each x in nums:
    result = result XOR x   (pairs cancel, the lone value survives)
return result

missing_number.optimal:
result = n   (index n has no slot in the array)
for each index i:
    result = result XOR i
    result = result XOR nums[i]   (every present value cancels with its index)
return result

spiral_matrix.brute:
visited = rows x cols grid of false
row_step = [0, 1, 0, -1], col_step = [1, 0, -1, 0]   (right, down, left, up)
r = 0, c = 0, direction = 0, result = empty list
repeat rows * cols times:
    append matrix[r][c] to result, mark (r, c) visited
    next_r = r + row_step[direction], next_c = c + col_step[direction]
    if (next_r, next_c) is off the grid or visited:
        direction = (direction + 1) mod 4
        next_r = r + row_step[direction], next_c = c + col_step[direction]
    r = next_r, c = next_c
return result
spiral_matrix.optimal:
result = empty list
top = 0, bottom = rows - 1, left = 0, right = cols - 1
while top <= bottom and left <= right:
    for each c from left to right: append matrix[top][c]
    top = top + 1
    for each r from top to bottom: append matrix[r][right]
    right = right - 1
    if top <= bottom:   (a row is still left, else the top row would repeat)
        for each c from right down to left: append matrix[bottom][c]
        bottom = bottom - 1
    if left <= right:
        for each r from bottom down to top: append matrix[r][left]
        left = left + 1
return result
